design: Durable dedup and watermark: the Kafka topic (acks=all, idempotent producer) is the durable journal. CanonicalEventBackbone keeps _seen_idempotency_keys and _last_sequence only as a cache of it, flagged by _recovered. Recovery reads earliest and latest offsets of every partition (kafka-get-offsets --time -2 / -1), consumes exactly the retained records and rebuilds keys and the maximum sequence per (governed_context_digest, aggregate_ref). This choice needs no new store or dependency and keeps the state consistent with what is actually durable (LLD v1.1 section 6 'deduplica durable').

When recovery runs: before an instance's first publish (restart), and after any KafkaBackboneError from the write, whose outcome is unknown. initialize() creates the topic with --create, which fails on an existing topic, so a just-created journal is known empty and needs no read.

Atomicity: publish() takes one threading.Lock around recovery, dedup check, ordering check, real Kafka write and state update. Schema and context guards stay before the lock (no shared state). Publishes through one instance are serialized (one console-producer call at a time).

EventOperationsCoordinator: one threading.Lock around the quota read/check/increment, around the decrement in finally, and around the per-event attempt counter; the backbone publish itself runs outside that lock.

findings_scope.K1: fixed: dedup check, real Kafka write and state update run under one per-instance lock; a concurrent identical publish finds the key recorded and is a no-op
findings_scope.K2: fixed: the ordering check and watermark update run under the same lock; the watermark never regresses and the late lower sequence is OUT_OF_ORDER
findings_scope.Q1: fixed: EventOperationsCoordinator reads, checks and increments the per-tenant in-flight count under one lock and decrements it under the same lock in finally, only after its own increment, so it never exceeds the quota and never goes negative, including on publish failure
findings_scope.R1: fixed: the topic is the durable journal; an instance rebuilds (governed_context_digest, idempotency_key) dedup keys from every record on the topic before its first publish, so a replay after restart is a no-op
findings_scope.R2: fixed: the same recovery rebuilds the per-(governed_context_digest, aggregate_ref) watermark as the maximum recorded sequence; a non-advancing sequence after restart is OUT_OF_ORDER
findings_scope.class_check: EventOperationsCoordinator's per-event attempt counter (POISON threshold) is the same read-modify-write class and is now updated under the same lock; dead letters and poison set use single atomic appends/adds
findings_scope.fail_closed: an unreadable journal record, a missing topic or an offsets answer naming no partition of the topic raise KafkaBackboneError before any write; there is no fallback to empty state
findings_scope.unchanged: C5 replay semantics (INFO-A option 1: same-context replay a safe no-op, no same-key/different-payload detection); REM-0025 isolation scoping of dedup and ordering (recovered state is keyed identically); envelope fields, Kafka record key and partitioning; quota/DLQ/poison/operator-gate behaviour without concurrency; public signatures
findings_scope.unknown_write_outcome: a failed Kafka write (KafkaBackboneError) marks the state unrecovered: the next publish rebuilds it from the journal, so a lost acknowledgement followed by a retry never writes a duplicate

inputs_tree_definition: git rev-parse <commit>:inputs (tree della directory inputs/ immutabile)
normative_interpretations: LLD v1.1 section 6 'C4/C5: ordering per aggregate/partition; watermark monotono; deduplica durable': the C5 watermark is the per-aggregate sequence state (INFO-C record), durable means it survives an instance restart; section 2.5 'Backpressure applica quote per tenant' is a bound on concurrent in-flight publishes per tenant, so it must hold under concurrency.

Scope of atomicity: per backbone instance. The instance is the single active producer of its topic; LLD v1.1 section 1.5/2.3 make the C3 outbox relay the single writer of canonical events. Two live instances publishing to one topic at the same time are not serialized with each other (see residual_risks); sequential hand-over between instances is covered by the recovery.

requirement_results.command: a new backbone instance on the same real broker and topic rebuilds dedup from the journal: replaying an already-durable idempotency_key is a no-op (exactly one record by Kafka end offsets), a new key is published once and then deduplicated (RED on c0bbf8a: the replay after restart wrote a second record)

after a restart a lower or equal sequence for the aggregate is quarantined OUT_OF_ORDER and never reaches the topic; an advancing sequence is accepted and advances the watermark, which a further restart recovers (RED on c0bbf8a: stale sequence 4 and equal sequence 5 accepted after restart)

recovered state stays keyed by governed_context_digest: after a restart another context reusing the key and aggregate is published, the same-context replay is a no-op, stale sequences of each aggregate of context A are OUT_OF_ORDER (RED on c0bbf8a: stale sequences accepted after restart)

a non-canonical record on the journal, a topic that does not exist, or an offsets answer naming no partition of the topic make publish fail closed with KafkaBackboneError, repeatedly, publishing nothing and quarantining nothing: never a fallback to empty state (RED on c0bbf8a: DID NOT RAISE for the first two; the third, a local failure-handling instrument over the real offsets query, was added after the first mutation probe and has no RED because the guarded branch is new)

fault injection on the real write: after a lost acknowledgement the retry of the same envelope is a no-op (state rebuilt from the journal) and the watermark holds; a write that never reached the broker is published exactly once on retry (RED on c0bbf8a: the lost-ACK retry wrote a duplicate, sequences [1, 2, 2]; the never-reached case is a positive control and passes there too)

two real threads publish the same envelope while the first Kafka write is held until the second publish has arrived: exactly one record; three distinct concurrent events are all written (RED on c0bbf8a: two records for one idempotency_key; the distinct-events case is a positive control)

sequence 5 is held inside its Kafka write while sequence 4 arrives: 4 is quarantined OUT_OF_ORDER, the topic holds [3, 5] and the watermark stays 5 in the instance and after a restart (RED on c0bbf8a: both accepted)

with the counter read held until a competing read is possible and admitted publishes held in flight until every caller is resolved: quota 1 admits exactly one of two, quota 2 admits two of three and refuses the third BACKPRESSURE_EXCEEDED; the counter never exceeds the quota, never goes negative and returns to 0 after governed rejections and a backend write failure (RED on c0bbf8a: both admitted, counter -1)
two concurrent failing publishes of one event record attempts 1 and 2, never 1 and 1, so the POISON threshold counts every attempt (RED on c0bbf8a: attempts [1, 1])

residual_risks: Two concurrently live backbone instances on one topic are not serialized with each other: each recovers the journal once, so a record written by the other after that point is not seen until the next unknown write outcome or restart. Cross-instance exclusion (Kafka transactions with fencing or a durable lock) is outside REM-0026 (acceptance criteria: restart and in-instance concurrency); the PoC has one producer per topic.

Recovery reads every retained record of the topic once per instance start: cost grows with the topic. A signed checkpoint bounding the replay (LLD v1.1 section 2.5 'Checkpoint lega topic/partition/offset') is not introduced here.

Records removed by Kafka retention are no longer deduplicated after a restart (recovery starts from the earliest retained offset). The PoC topics use the broker default retention; no retention-aware dedup store is introduced.
Publishes through one instance are serialized by the lock (one console-producer call at a time): bounded throughput in the PoC, acceptable for the component's role; not a performance claim.
Same-key/different-payload reuse inside one context is still dropped as a replay without quarantine or audit (INFO-A option 1, note for a future normative decision).
CanonicalEventBackbone and EventOperationsCoordinator are not yet used by other ocor-runtime modules (INFO-A/INFO-C audits); G6 ingestion qualification (BA-07, FR-069..FR-075) depends on them.
Pre-existing unlabelled ocor-c5-backbone-data-* volumes from 2026-10-05/2026-10-10 are not created by this session and were not touched.
